nodes.summary: A pattern whose crashes happen before round `T`, at most one per round, has at most `T` faulty processes.
nodes.title: An admissible pattern has at most `T` faulty processes

nodes.summary: `π j = some (ρ, D)` when process `j` crashes in round `ρ`, its messages of that round reaching exactly the processes of `D`; `π j = none` when `j` is correct.
nodes.title: Crash pattern

nodes.summary: A protocol for the processes `G` with inputs in `V`, local states `σ` and messages `M`. Process `i` starts in state `init i x` from its input `x`; in round `r` process `j` in state `s` sends `send r j s i` to process `i`, and process `i` in state `s` moves to `recv r i s msg`, where `msg j` is the message it received from `j`, or `none` if it received none; at the end process `i` decides `decide i s`.
nodes.title: Synchronous protocol with crash failures

nodes.summary: The round in which a process crashes, `0` if it does not.
nodes.title: Crash round

nodes.summary: The value process `i` decides after `T` rounds.
nodes.title: Decision under crash failures

nodes.summary: If `π j = none`, every message of `j` is delivered.
nodes.title: A correct process delivers every message

nodes.summary: Whether the message of `j` to `i` in round `r` is delivered: always if `j` is correct; if `j` crashes in round `ρ` with recipients `D`, exactly when `r < ρ`, or `r = ρ` and `i ∈ D`.
nodes.title: Message delivery under a crash pattern

nodes.summary: If there are at least $f + 2$ processes and at least two values, and a deterministic synchronous protocol solves consensus (agreement and validity, every correct process deciding at the end of round $T$) tolerating $f$ crash failures, then $T \ge f + 1$.
nodes.title: Consensus with $f$ crash failures needs $f + 1$ rounds

nodes.summary: The processes that crash.
nodes.title: Faulty processes of a crash pattern

nodes.summary: Every crash happens in one of the rounds `0, …, T - 1`, and at most one process crashes in each round.
nodes.title: Admissible crash pattern for `T` rounds

nodes.summary: Faulty processes are those that crash.
nodes.title: Faulty processes are those that crash

nodes.summary: If there are at least $T + 2$ processes and at least two values, no deterministic synchronous protocol solves consensus in $T$ rounds against the crash patterns whose crashes happen before round $T$, at most one per round. This is Theorem 1 of Aguilera and Toueg (1999) with $t = T$: "Consider a synchronous round-based system S with n processes and at most t crash failures such that at most one process crashes in…
nodes.title: Consensus against $T$ crashes, at most one per round, needs more than $T$ rounds

nodes.summary: With at least two processes and at least two values, no protocol solves consensus in zero rounds, even when no process crashes: each process would decide a function of its own input, validity forces that function to be the identity, and two processes with different inputs then disagree. This is the case $f = 0$ of the $f + 1$ round lower bound.
nodes.title: Consensus needs a round

nodes.summary: If `Q` solves consensus in $T$ rounds against every crash pattern with at most $f$ faulty processes, and $T \le f$, then it solves consensus against every pattern with crashes before round $T$, at most one per round.
nodes.title: Solving consensus against $f \ge T$ crashes includes one crash per round

nodes.summary: `Q` solves consensus in `T` rounds against every admissible crash pattern for `T` rounds (crashes before round `T`, at most one per round): no two correct processes decide differently, and the value decided by a correct process is the input of some process. This is the system of Aguilera and Toueg's Theorem 1.
nodes.title: Solving consensus against at most one crash per round

nodes.summary: `Q` solves consensus tolerating `f` crashes in `T` rounds: for all inputs and every crash pattern with at most `f` faulty processes, no two correct processes decide differently (agreement), and the value decided by a correct process is the input of some process (validity).
nodes.title: Solving consensus with crash failures

nodes.summary: States agree up to round `k` when the deliveries of the rounds before `k` agree.
nodes.title: Executions agree while deliveries agree

nodes.summary: From round `k₀` on, let the process `q` deliver nothing in two executions, let the other processes deliver alike, and let the processes other than `q` be in equal states at round `k₀`. Then the processes other than `q` stay in equal states.
nodes.title: A silent process changes nothing for the others

nodes.summary: A process's next state depends only on the current states and on what it receives.
nodes.title: One round of an execution under crash failures

nodes.summary: `Q.state x π r i` is the state of process `i` after `r` rounds of `Q` with inputs `x` and crash pattern `π`.
nodes.title: Executions under crash failures

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
